standard_prerequisites.name: Injective module and the pullback-pushforward adjunction
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the adjunction between f^* and f_* on modules, and the extension property of injective modules

core_obligations: Use the adjunction (proof lines 2265-2268): for a monomorphism of O_D-modules the pullback is a monomorphism because f is flat, and the adjunction identifies maps into f_*I with maps into I.
Conclude injectivity (proof lines 2268-2270): the extension property of the injective module I transfers across the adjunction, so f_*I is injective.
proof_roadmap: Pull back a monomorphism and use flatness to keep it a monomorphism.
Transfer the extension property of I across the adjunction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the pushforward of an injective module along a flat morphism of ringed topoi is injective (statement lines 2256-2263). The proof uses the pullback-pushforward adjunction together with exactness of the pullback, which is the flatness hypothesis, to transfer the extension property defining injectivity (proof lines 2265-2270). The non-formal content is the placement of the flatness hypothesis: it is needed precisely to keep monomorphisms monomorphisms after pullback. The claim is H2: one adjunction argument.
